newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn's Ruehe shrugs off new Eurofighter doubts.
newsitem.headline: Bonn's Ruehe shrugs off new Eurofighter doubts.

text.p: Defence Minister Volker Ruehe on Thursday said Germany would participate in the Eurofighter project as planned, rejecting comments by a Finance Ministry official that defence budgets must be cut.

Ruehe repeated that he had received pledges from Finance Minister Theo Waigel on German participation in the four-nation project and said Finance Ministry State Secretary Manfred Overhaus was not in a position make such comments.
"A state secretary is not partner to such discussions," Ruehe told reporters in Bonn, adding that his contacts had been with Waigel and Chancellor Helmut Kohl.
Overhaus told a Defence Ministry committee on Wednesday that the ministry, along with other government departments, had to make budget savings as part of an austerity drive in Germany.
Ruehe told journalists that in earlier budget discussions he had already promised to redirect some of his budget to ensure Germany was part of the fighter-plane project.
The jet is being jointly developed by Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG, British Aerospace, Spain's CASA and Italy's Alenia.
Ruehe said last week after talks with British Defence Minister George Robertson he expected a decision next month when the German cabinet is due to consider next year's budget.
The project is estimated to cost Germany a total 23 billion marks ($13.5 billion).
